A female character who IS the element; her costume, ornaments and colors carry the element’s traits. Both hands are ordinary human hands and hold nothing.

Behind her, a richly painted background with layered painterly colour, subtle visible brushwork, atmospheric perspective and cinematic depth. Luminous, rich colours; crisp focal details on the face and costume, softer painted edges toward the distance.
Face proportions: a short midface and a soft, gently rounded jawline with a small soft chin; any crown or headpiece sits above her hairline. Her eyes keep the shape and size described below.

2. CHARACTER

Face — her own: a sharp, striking, intense look; fair skin; delicate V-line face with a small, soft chin; eyes on the larger side of natural — almond-shaped eyes of natural size, level outer eye corners; gracefully arched brows; petite straight nose; lips with a defined cupid's bow, of natural size; steel-blue eyes; a small beauty mark under one eye.

Her element, carried in her design: berkelium: a soft silvery synthetic metal first made in late 1949 by striking americium with alpha particles, and named for the university town where she was born, just as terbium above her was named for a small village; the town itself was named for a philosopher who taught that to exist is to be perceived, and at first she existed only as the decay of a few atoms, until more than a decade later a speck large enough to see was gathered; in water she turns yellow and pale green, and in 2009 a few precious milligrams of her, gathered over months in a reactor, were flown across an ocean to another laboratory to become the target that made element 117.

Costume: she is a female mecha personification — plates, joints, binders and glow lines carry the traits above; the plates must read as solid armor with visible joints, not as cloth or a gown; a back unit may carry the motif. Light deep-navy and chalk-white armor with fine gold trim, several small shield-shaped drone units floating symmetrically around her like a study group, each cradling a tiny sealed capsule glowing pale yellow-green, a small bell-tower-shaped gold core at the chest; the plates must read as solid armor, not a gown.
Silhouette: light body armor with several small shield and drone units floating symmetrically around her. Only the overall shape is fixed; design the details freely in the element's materials and palette.
Colours: scholar's deep navy, tassel gold, berkelium-salt pale yellow-green, chalk-white stone.
Exposure (bold): her mecha frame is cut open by design in only these places — bare shoulders and upper arms between pauldron and gauntlet, and a deep open chest window with natural cleavage framed by the chest plates; everywhere else she stays fully plated. The plates stay on, fitted and symmetrical, with skin clearly showing in each opening. Nothing slipped off. Intimate areas covered; keep the plate material and palette.

4. SCENE
World: year 2200, an academy city of floating lecture halls: seminar islands hovering above a bay linked by bridges of light, a giant accelerator ring circling beneath the hills, and a courier dock where swarms of small drones carry sealed sample capsules to laboratories on other continents.
Pose: standing confidently, her body turned slightly while her face looks toward the viewer.
Light: the scene's own light, rendered the way this style renders light and skin.
Composition: vertical 2:3 full-body framing with modest headroom and clear space below the boots — the whole figure from the top of her head or headpiece to both feet stays inside the frame, occupying about four-fifths of the image height, with the same camera distance in every world; her hands stay inside the frame. Camera level with her face with natural portrait perspective; her head level, chin neither raised nor tucked — no upward perspective on her face, no wide-angle distortion, no low angle, no close crop.

5. CONSTRAINTS
One figure only; no text or numbers except her element's own chemical symbol (Bk) and atomic number (97) — and those only as part of the scene: engraved, embroidered or glowing on her costume, a banner, a sign or a machine, never as a floating label, corner badge, periodic-table tile, caption or overlay on the picture; no logo or watermark.
Avoid: flat single-tone cel shading, photographic appearance, semi-realistic face, plastic 3D-render finish.
